evidence.note: The variable defaults to true (environ.py:1348@297e54fd) and only chooses whether DeepGEMM's JIT kernels serve the fp8 GEMMs that have them (deep_gemm_wrapper/configurer.py:35-55: off returns False before the device and import checks, so the Triton and cuBLAS paths run). A run that exports it at true states the default, so its pool resolves, lowers and schedules as one that does not state it. The engine reads the variable from the pool's engine block env map (sglangengine.TestTheEngineReadsItsEnvironmentFromTheEnvMap): true is accepted and changes no decision; false is refused by name, because it would run other kernels than the ones the registry's coefficients were measured on. Named substitution: no DeepGEMM kernel is priced separately from the registry's fp8 GEMM entries, so a point that states true is priced as every point is.

approximates.evidence: the registry's attention coefficients are fitted per part on the model graph's sparse-MLA lane and are not keyed by the DSA backend; no allowed table measures flashmla_sparse, flashmla_kv, trtllm or fa3 sparse attention separately for this model on this part
approximates.differs: the decode backend the engine runs is a different kernel (flashmla_sparse, flashmla_kv, trtllm or fa3, layers/attention/dsa/ at SGLang v0.5.23) with its own latency; the cost model prices the part-wide attention pair whichever is stated, so the step time of a DSA model carries the difference between that pair and the stated kernel
